To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a method that provides an unbiased and automatic implementation of regularization mechanisms on sampled data, with a biological plausibility.

1) we have defined a method to derive a discrete filter from a continuous differential operator, 2) the method is automatic and unbiased, 3) it leads to a filter architecture which is biologically plausible, and 4) the method is illustrated by two applications in computer vision: visual motion estimation and image denoising.

(i) we provide a method for deriving an optimal implementation of a continuous regularization process on discrete data, which is unbiased and which corresponds to the observed cortical architecture, (ii) this method allows to obtain an optimal implementation of the continuous regularization process, which is unbiased.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of algorithms for the regularization of vectorial quantities in vision.
the development of a general framework for the implementation of regularization mechanisms on sampled data and the study of its properties.
the development and implementation of regularization mechanisms in computer vision and in the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present development provides a general framework for the implementation of regularization mechanisms in a biologically plausible way.
the method provides an unbiased, automatic and biologically plausible implementation of regularization mechanisms.
the present development provides an optimal and unbiased implementation of any continuous regularization mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the present development provides a new and powerful tool for regularization mechanisms in computer or biological vision.
it is possible to define a regularization mechanism on continuous quantities and then derive a non-linear discrete filter that implements the regularization without introducing any bias.
we provide here a general framework for the implementation of regularization processes, and we show its application to two important problems in computer and biological vision.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed implementation is a general and unbiased method to compute the solution of any partial differential equation, which is a major improvement with respect to the existing methods.

the proposed method provides a simple and efficient tool for the design and implementation of regularization mechanisms for vectorial maps in computer vision and in the study of the brain visual system.
the present method allows to implement any regularization mechanism in an unbiased manner, which is of interest for many applications in computer and biological vision.
